read_sources: canonical WEB Nahum coordinates and text
not_read: state or completion artifacts for Nah

non_authority_statement: Candidate literary and structural evidence only. Every boundary is LOW and deferred_human_or_external_ai. No theology, canon, authorship, date, historicity, ethics, identity, fulfillment, preferred witness, preferred reading, preferred translation, source tradition, graph, retrieval, reviewed-gold, or promotion authority.
routing_principle: Prefer larger coherent poems and rhetorical movements. Preserve the opening theophanic poem, alternating enemy/refuge addresses, herald-feast hinge, sustained siege tableau, lion taunt, woe-city exposure, Thebes comparison, futile-defense locust swarm, and closing king-lament. Alphabetic, lexical, versification, and translation observations are evidence only.

macro_parent_alternatives.form: superscription, theophanic poem, alternating enemy/refuge speech, and peace-herald closure
macro_parent_alternatives.preservation_reason: The opening chapter moves from vision title through divine-character poem to addressed consequences and a climactic feast command.

macro_parent_alternatives.form: scatterer summons, restoration rationale, siege tableau, devastation, and lion-den taunt
macro_parent_alternatives.preservation_reason: Rapid commands and battle images culminate in emptiness before the lion metaphor and final opposition formula.

macro_parent_alternatives.form: woe-city indictment, exposure, Thebes comparison, futile preparations, swarm satire, and closing lament
macro_parent_alternatives.preservation_reason: The final chapter sustains direct address through comparison, mock counsel, vanishing officials, and incurable-wound closure.

global_hot_zones.issue: A debated partial or disrupted alphabetic pattern can invite reconstruction or atomization.
global_hot_zones.handling: Keep the whole theophanic/refuge poem together; make no reconstructed text, source-layer, or preferred-reading claim.

global_hot_zones.issue: Refuge, flood, enemy pursuit, and direct question allow competing seams.
global_hot_zones.handling: Retain 1:7-8 within the opening poem and preserve 1:2-9 and 1:7-15 as larger alternatives.

global_hot_zones.issue: Pronoun, addressee, quotation, and number shifts are difficult to reproduce transparently in English.
global_hot_zones.handling: Keep the enemy/decree movement large and defer addressee and translation resolution.

global_hot_zones.issue: Hebrew and common English chapter numbering place pressure around the herald and scatterer sequence.
global_hot_zones.handling: Use received WEB coordinates, preserve 1:15-2:2 as an exact alternative, and make no versification or textual authority claim.

global_hot_zones.issue: The palace-collapse and carried-away wording contains translation and referent uncertainty.
global_hot_zones.handling: Retain inside the full siege tableau; do not isolate a lexeme or prefer a rendering.

global_hot_zones.issue: Sexualized city metaphor, exposure, and shame imagery carry ethical and interpretive risk.
global_hot_zones.handling: Keep accusation and announced exposure together as rhetoric; make no ethical or identity adjudication.

global_hot_zones.issue: No-Amon/Thebes naming, geography, historical comparison, and violent imagery invite chronology and fulfillment claims.
global_hot_zones.handling: Treat the named-city comparison as literary evidence only and keep comparison through application.

global_hot_zones.issue: Imperatives, fire/sword, grasshopper-locust terms, and official titles permit multiple stanza divisions and translations.
global_hot_zones.handling: Preserve the whole futile-defense and swarm movement while retaining 3:14-15 and 3:16-17 as exact alternatives.

units.title: Vision-book superscription
units.deciding_marker: Revelation, book, vision, named prophet, and named subject jointly introduce the work before the Yahweh poem begins.
units.rejected_alternative: Merging the title into the theophany or treating its labels as authorship or genre-history proof.
units.risk: authorship, title terminology, Nineveh identity, and vision ontology

units.title: Yahweh the avenger, storm ruler, refuge, and pursuer
units.literary_form: theophanic character poem with rhetorical question and refuge contrast
units.deciding_marker: Repeated divine name and vengeance terms expand through storm, sea, land, mountain, fire, refuge, flood, and darkness before direct plotting address.
units.rejected_alternative: Reconstructing alphabetic order, isolating 1:7 as a maxim, or detaching 1:8 from the contrast.
units.risk: acrostic reconstruction, divine attributes, violence, creation imagery, and translation

units.title: Plotters ended and yoke broken
units.literary_form: direct challenge, enemy images, paired decree, and liberation oracle
units.deciding_marker: Plot question, full-end refrain, thorn/stubble image, evil counselor, Yahweh-speech formula, yoke breaking, and name/grave decree form one alternating-address movement.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting at every addressee shift or deciding whether each pronoun denotes Judah, Nineveh, a ruler, or another referent.
units.risk: speaker and addressee ambiguity, pronouns, quotation scope, idols, violence, and translation

units.title: Peace herald and feast command
units.deciding_marker: Behold, mountain feet, good news, peace, feast keeping, vow performance, and no-more-passing form a compact hinge before the scatterer command.
units.rejected_alternative: Treating the verse in isolation from its enemies-ended context or resolving its cross-chapter versification pressure.
units.risk: versification, addressee, liturgy, later canonical reuse, and fulfillment

units.title: Scatterer summons and restoration rationale
units.literary_form: urgent defense commands with explanatory restoration hinge
units.deciding_marker: The arriving scatterer and four imperatives are followed by a for-clause about restored majesty and ruined vines before the battle tableau begins.
units.rejected_alternative: Separating 2:2 as a doctrinal promise or merging the commands into every following siege detail.
units.risk: speaker, irony, Jacob-Israel language, restoration, translation, and versification

units.title: Assault, breach, flight, plunder, and desolation
units.literary_form: kinetic siege tableau and devastation climax
units.deciding_marker: Red shields, rushing chariots, wall advance, river gates, palace collapse, lamenting attendants, flight, plunder commands, and threefold emptiness sustain one accelerating scene.
units.rejected_alternative: Atomizing vehicle images, palace collapse, flight, plunder, or bodily terror into independent chunks.
units.risk: historicity, military imagery, gendered city imagery, translation, violence, and fulfillment

units.title: Where is the lions' den?
units.literary_form: lion-den taunt and concluding opposition oracle
units.deciding_marker: Where-question recalls fearless lions and accumulated prey; the opposition formula answers with burned chariots, devoured cubs, ended prey, and silenced messengers.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting the lion recollection from its answering oracle or deciding the metaphor's historical referents.
units.risk: metaphorical identity, imperial critique, violence, messengers, and fulfillment

units.title: Woe to the bloody city and public exposure
units.literary_form: woe indictment, battle soundscape, causal accusation, exposure oracle, and no-comfort question
units.deciding_marker: Woe names the city; whip/wheel/horse/sword sounds accumulate bodies; because introduces accusation; opposition formula announces exposure; spectators flee and ask who will mourn.
units.rejected_alternative: Separating battle catalogue from its because-clause or isolating exposure imagery from the accusation and no-mourner closure.
units.risk: violence, sexualized metaphor, shame, nations, ethics, and identity

units.title: Thebes comparison applied to Nineveh
units.literary_form: rhetorical city comparison, defeat account, and second-person application
units.deciding_marker: Are-you-better question introduces No-Amon's waters and allies, proceeds through captivity, then repeats you-also and extends the comparison through drunkenness, fragile forts, open gates, and fire.
units.rejected_alternative: Detaching the Thebes account from its you-also application or using the comparison to settle date and fulfillment.
units.risk: place-name translation, geography, chronology, nations, gendered language, violence, and fulfillment

units.title: Futile fortress work and vanishing swarm
units.literary_form: mock preparation commands, reversal, multiplication taunt, and locust simile
units.deciding_marker: Commands to draw water, strengthen, and make bricks meet fire and sword; repeated multiply language expands into merchants, guards, and officials who strip or disappear like locusts.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting the preparation commands from their reversal or isolating merchants and officials as unrelated catalogues.
units.risk: imperative irony, fire and sword, insect terminology, official-title translation, commerce, and history

units.title: Sleeping shepherds and incurable royal wound
units.literary_form: direct-address closing lament and international taunt response
units.deciding_marker: King-of-Assyria vocative, sleeping shepherds, scattered people, no gatherer, no healing, fatal wound, report hearing, handclap, and final rhetorical question close the book.
units.rejected_alternative: Separating failed leadership from the wound verdict or converting the closing question into a theological or historical adjudication.
units.risk: royal identity, shepherd metaphor, death imagery, corporate judgment, history, and fulfillment
